citation: Provider cites J. Baek and A. B. Birchfield, Dynamic performance design and validation in large, IBR-heavy synthetic grids, Energies 18(15), July 2025. Paper not independently reviewed.
description: Texas A&M University provides a synthetic electricity-grid model for the greater Memphis region and the New Madrid Seismic Area, developed for the DOE All-Hazards project. Its geographic coverage extends from 34 to 38 degrees north and from 88 to 92 degrees west. It describes 11,186 MW of peak load in four areas, 63 generating plants with 188 units, and 19,628 MW of combined nameplate capacity derived from the 2024 EIA-860 report. The network contains 974 AC transmission lines and 407 transformers. Dynamic models support stability analysis. The provider states that the network was designed for N-1 AC power-flow contingency security; that claim was not independently tested here. The case supports power-flow and resilience studies, but it does not represent the actual Memphis grid. The catalogue describes it as approximately 1,000 buses. The case page provides a download form with a required email field. Texas A&M permits free commercial and non-commercial use under its stated terms and encourages citation. The specific file formats and archive contents remain unverified because no model files were downloaded. Related cases are available through the Texas A&M Electric Grid Test Case Repository.
